note:
NUBA — Tetouan 1790. Muhammad al-Ha'ik's *kunnash*, the songbook
compiled in Tetouan at the end of the eighteenth century that wrote
down the eleven surviving Andalusi nubat and is the reason there are
eleven rather than none. Twenty-four were counted in the medieval
sources; the other thirteen were already lost when he wrote.
IT IS THE SAME KIND OF ROW AS `counterpoint`: a codification, dated
by the book, sitting on a practice that runs back through the
Maghribi courts to Ziryab's Cordoba in the ninth century — and this
block dates it by the book on purpose, with the comment saying so,
which is the repair `counterpoint` needed.
WHAT IT DOES NOT PAY. `troubadour` wants "andalusi song" and `fado`
wants "moorish andalusi song", and this row is NOT either of them:
both want the twelfth-century music of al-Andalus itself, and this
is its North African survival codified six hundred years later. Both
wants stay open. Paying them with this would be the conscription
WORLD.md §4 names.
THE AXES: FORM is the identity and it is the one this box cannot
hold. A nuba is five movements in five different metres, each
starting slow and accelerating into the next. What ships is one
movement of it, said plainly in the row's `cannot`.

LINEAGE: a declared ROOT for the same reason `taqsim` is one —
the ancestor is Andalusi court music and there is no anchor for
it, and there will not be one until somebody can name a place, a
year and a source for it that is not this book.
"andalusi's cordoban court music" PAID 2026-08-29 (Córdoba 822):
al-Ha'ik's Tetouan songbook is that school's repertory written
down after the expulsions carried it to the Maghreb — the
tradition's own account of itself, now sayable as an edge.
"muwashshah" stays on the books: the strophic form's identity is
its aksak metres and no named dated source predates its
dependents (the genealogy round's declined list).
"muwashshah" PAID 2026-08-30 (Cairo 1200) — the comment below
said it stayed on the books because "no named dated source
predates its dependents"; Dar at-Tiraz predates this row by six
centuries and the sentence is defeated, not argued around. The
nuba's own repertory IS muwashshah texts by the hundred.

THE MODE THIS RECORD CANNOT SOUND (2026-09-02, the catalogue round,
shift 2; test/precompose.test.js G14b).
Muhammad al-Ha'ik's KUNNASH, compiled at Tetouan at the end of the
eighteenth century — this row's own book, place and (dated-by-the-book)
year. The eleven surviving nubat are in the Maghribi TUBU', which this box
cannot spell: the row is `harmony: "modal"` and the mode reached nothing.
Rather than leave a Greek mode-name standing in for a tab' nobody here has
measured, the field names the plain alphabet the row actually plays. The
tubu' stay in the row's `cannot`, where an unplayable fact belongs.

the tar and darbuka's basic cycle, voiced on what there is: a
frame-drum stroke on the beat and the tar's rattle between.

WHO SINGS: `trobar` — a chant-trained tenor, open vowels,
more breath than a church allows, one syllable a beat.
The row was written for Provence 1210 and the joke is that
it is right here for a reason: that is the direction the
borrowing actually ran.

THE DYNAMIC FIGURE (2026-09-06, the dynamics flood, shift 1): `dyn:
"agogic"` — the line leans on its last note. The Arab court line arrives
at its phrase end, ancestor and descendant alike. The `roots` cluster
takes `lean`; the anchor's own evidence outranks it, which is the
flood's rule (docs/DYNAMICS-FLOOD.md).

cannot: the five mayazin — a nuba runs basit, qaim wa nisf, btayhi, darj, insiraf and quddam, in 6/4, 8/4, 4/4, 5/8 and 6/8, each accelerating to a khalas; an anchor cannot declare a metre at all in this table and one record has one tempo (WORLD.md §2 walls 1 and 2, neither landed)

the orchestra — no oud, no rabab, no qanun, no tar. The fiddle below is a violin played on the knee in the real thing, which is at least the same instrument; the rest are cognates and the harp is a guess at a qanun
words: the chorus, singing the sana'a in unison
